acceptanceCriteria: A focused test reproduces a plan row whose BASE span is outside every hunk but whose text recurs in an added region, and asserts the refusal's fix line states the cause.
The DCW spec documents the cause wording under the cite-span-not-stable reason.
The existing refusal code and exit status are unchanged.
body: Observed 2026-10-13 on lane V1-1303 (branch claude/v1-1303-stable-sidecar-reuse, base 94a7d3dc53e1314e761bc306dda80d338d2e2ed6, PR beamfall/corvint#856), Core build from origin/main. The first citation plan was refused `cem-cite NOT_PRODUCED cite-span-not-stable` on row 7, span docs/specs/cem-stable-v1.md:1413:1415. Those BASE lines sit outside every diff hunk, but their text (`Acceptance evidence:` and a table header) is repeated by the new section the change adds, so the stability check treated the span as edited. Expected: the fix line names the reason (for example that the span's content also occurs inside a changed region, or that the span moved) and the nearest stable alternative. Actual: the refusal names only the row and span, so the builder had to find a unique line by trial (citing requirement lines 1331..1401 worked). Relation to DCW-V0-019/DCW-V0-046 to be confirmed by the implementer.
title: dogfood change: cite-span-not-stable should say why a span outside every hunk counts as edited
